text:
maya: pushed a small rate-policy tweak to prod ~10m ago (canary 15%) and now seeing a 4-6% uptick in 429s for some customers in us-west-2. not sure if burst window math is off.

alex: which policy did you change? can you paste the policy id + commit?

maya: policy id rp-v2-2026-03, commit 9f3b7a2. changed per-user burst from 120->80 tokens for safety on sustained traffic.

jun: oye, lowering burst could make short spikes hit quota faster. do we have pre/post hist on token distribution for the affected keys?

maya: quick diff and prometheus spikes attached below (copy):
```
# diff
- user_burst: 120
+ user_burst: 80
```
prom: increase in 429 rate starting at 1718208600, concentrated at 99th pct -> clients with short-lived fanout.

ops-bot: Deploy notice: rp-v2-2026-03 applied to prod (canary 15%). rollout id: r-roll-332.

alex: ok canary 15% is supposed to catch this. two options: widen burst back to 120 for canary or roll back the change entirely. i'd vote widen and monitor for downstream cost impact.

sara: customers flagged via #support are getting paged. @cs-lead FYI. we should triage top 3 affected orgs.

jun: can repro locally with a simple fanout script. run this to reproduce 429 quickly:
```
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":20}' &\
  sleep 0.02; \
done
```
I hit 429s after ~40 concurrent inflight on the lowered burst.

maya: thanks. i'm gonna patch canary to 110 for the moment while we decide. leaving rollback as last resort.

alex: if you patch canary, flip the rollout percentage to 0 and reapply with new config so we don't have split-state. also add a canary metric check for 429 rate < 0.5% over 5m.

maya: doing now. command: `rollout update r-roll-332 --canary-config user_burst=110 --percent=15`

deploy-bot: rollout r-roll-332 update accepted by maya. job 4482 queued.

ops-bot: metric alert silenced for this thread; keep an eye.

sara: I'll open a quick ticket with Customer Success for the three customers, include repro steps and mitigation.

jun: after patch, i'll run the fanout load against the canary endpoints (15% of traffic) and post results.

maya: patch applied, canary now user_burst=110.

jun: running repro... 1m run: 429s down to baseline ~0.2% from 5%. looks good for canary.

alex: sounds like safe temp fix. let's schedule a brief retro to decide final numbers. also add a note to the runbook about "short fanout workloads" and baseline burst recommendations.

maya: agreed. i'll prepare a rollback play if the rate creeps back up. setting a 1h watch.

sara: CS ticket created: CS-4571, status: investigating, customers notified.

maya: resolution update in 1h or earlier. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks team. we can close when watch completes and CS confirms no more complaints.

maya: final update: watch passed, no spike seen after canary patch. leaving policy at 110 and opening a follow-up to test heavier fanout patterns in staging. closing thread.

sara: noted, filing follow-up ops action: increase staging fanout suite + add chaos scenario. :white_check_mark:
